Detailed Description

Adjective wordlist for ACDS session naming.

Defines a curated list of 2500 English adjectives used as the first component of memorable ACDS session identifiers (e.g., "blue-mountain-tiger").

Session String Format

ASCII Chat uses a 3-part session identifier for easy memorization and communication: 

adjective-noun-noun
Example: "blue-mountain-tiger"

This format provides approximately 2500 * 5000 * 5000 = 62.5 billion possible combinations, far exceeding the practical needs of a session discovery service.

Usage in ACDS

The ACDS (ASCII Chat Discovery Service) uses session strings for:

  • User-friendly session discovery without IP addresses
  • Memorable identifiers that can be shared verbally or written down
  • Privacy protection (no direct server IP exposure)

Generation flow:

1.
Server registers with ACDS, receives a unique session string
2.
Clients connect to ACDS and search for a session by its string
3.
ACDS returns the server's address for that session

Implementation Notes

  • Adjectives are selected for easy pronunciation and memorability
  • Random selection uses libsodium's randombytes_uniform() for cryptographic randomness
  • Total: 2500 adjectives (provides diversity while keeping generation fast)
  • This file is auto-generated by generate_wordlists.py; modify the generation script if changes to the wordlist are needed

Variable Documentation

const char* adjectives[]

Array of English adjectives for ACDS session naming. A curated list of 2500 adjectives used to generate the first part of memorable session identifiers. Combined with two nouns to create unique, pronounceable strings.

Example values: "blue", "bright", "calm", "dark", "eager", "fresh", "gentle", ...
